title: Replace tautological literal-vs-literal assertions in epic_15/epic_16 story-acceptance tests with real checks against the code under test
why: Each of these 8 test() blocks asserts a Dart-literal identity (0<=0, '${11}x'=='11x', Duration(milliseconds:800).inMilliseconds==800, 1>=1) or throws-and-catches a locally-constructed exception, instead of pumping ReviewCountBadge/AnimatedProgressBar, calling the satisfaction-message function, invoking the real manual-completion use case, or exercising reward-isolation logic. Every one of these is mathematically incapable of failing regardless of what the corresponding production code does: delete ReviewCountBadge, change the satisfaction-cue thresholds, or reintroduce a reward-isolation bug, and all 8 stay green. CI reports these ACs (16.4 badge/format, 16.6 progress-bar/satisfaction/animation, 15.11/15.16 reward-isolation/child-self-mark) as covered when they provide zero regression protection.
recommendation: For each site, either (a) pump/construct the real widget or call the real function and assert on its output, or (b) mark the test/group skip: with a reason, matching the convention this same file already uses for retired ACs (e.g. epic_15's 'ContentVersionCheckService removed' skips).
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 8 listed tests either asserts against a real widget/service call (ReviewCountBadge, AnimatedProgressBar, the satisfaction-cue function, the manual-completion use case, reward-isolation logic) or is skip:-wrapped with a stated reason.
No test in story_acceptance/ asserts a boolean/string/Duration literal against itself as its only check.
No deterministic Rule-0 checker exists for this pattern; verify by code review that each assertion's left-hand side traces to a call into lib/, not a value constructed entirely within the test.

corrections: expect(p1.id, isNot(p2.id)) (line 1318) calls real profileRepo.createProfile, so it's a weak/stale assertion (rewards feature removed, per its own comment) rather than a pure literal tautology like the other 7 — don't count it as 'mathematically incapable of failing.'

mergedFrom: Fix epic_16 AC-4/AC-7 tests asserting against a fabricated, already-drifted copy of the onboarding phase order
